The graph section found zero forests of order 10, 80 geometric forests of order 9, three peeling layers of sizes 4,4,1, exchange edges 280,280,920 with respective profiles (1,7),(1,7),(1,23,48,8), and 40 slide edges with profile (1,1).
correctness.rationale: The 16 characters on the even-parity group are represented without repetition by supports of sizes 0, 1 and 2. The generators flip all but one coordinate, so the respective eigenvalues are 5, −3 and 1. Parseval and the induced edge count give e(U)=m²/4−3m/2+Σbᵢⱼ²/8. At ten vertices this exceeds the forest bound; at nine each bᵢⱼ is odd, so eight edges are necessary and a forest forces all |bᵢⱼ|=1. The five odd coordinate sums then have squares summing to 53; the three listed patterns exhaust the possibilities. Two majority counts of seven would overlap in at least five points, impossible for two halfspaces; in the 7,6,6,6 majority-count case, the two points outside the 7-point majority agree on four coordinates and hence on all five. Thus only a full halfspace plus one point survives. The halfspace induces a matching; the outside point has one neighbor in each edge by triangle-freeness, giving the subdivided star. For the exchange rule, cross-index adjacency at cost three requires neither omitted point to lie in the intersection. The degree is 7+4·4. When both omissions block a cross-index move, they agree on a third coordinate by parity; opposite that bit, choose an omitted point with the opposite values on the two original coordinates, giving a common neighbor. States from complementary halfspaces cannot have a common neighbor because its omission would have to miss both; a third-clique route of length three exists using any coordinate on which the two original omissions agree. Token slides occur along just the four matching edges per halfspace. At threshold four the inactive induced graph is pruned at degree at most one, giving precisely three rounds on these trees.
residual_risks: All enumeration is on the specified degree-five graph. The exchange analysis does not allow sequential unit moves through intermediate optimum configurations when the exchange size is above one.
